cluster_summary: quoteIdentifierIfNecessary(vars[0]) is called with undefined when the SQL expression has no sibling query, so isValidIdentifier's toUpperCase throws a TypeError and the editor crashes on render where it previously rendered 'FROM undefined'.
rationale: With refIds empty vars[0] is undefined and isValidIdentifier calls identifier.toUpperCase() → TypeError during render, where it previously rendered 'FROM undefined'; exactly thread 0.
thread_body: initialQuery now calls quoteIdentifierIfNecessary(vars[0]). If there are no non-expression queries, refIds can be empty (ExpressionQueryEditor filters out the current query), making vars[0] undefined and causing a runtime crash when quoteIdentifierIfNecessary runs. Add a guard for the empty refIds/vars case (e.g., don’t generate an initial FROM clause / use a placeholder and skip auto-initialization) and add a regression test for mounting SqlExpr with an empty refIds array.

cluster_summary: metaSqlExpr.ts binds to a file-local regex-only quoteIdentifierIfNecessary with no reserved-word check while the other call sites use the mysql helper, so reserved-word refIds are quoted in the editor but left bare in the metadata query, which fails and silently empties column autocomplete.
rationale: metaSqlExpr.ts binds to a file-local regex-only quoteIdentifierIfNecessary (no reserved-word check) while SqlExpr/completion use the mysql helper, so a reserved-word refId is quoted in the editor but bare in the metadata query — precisely thread 2.
thread_body: Table quoting logic is inconsistent across the SQL expressions feature: this file uses the local quoteIdentifierIfNecessary (regex-only) while SqlExpr/autocomplete use the MySQL sqlUtil version (which also quotes reserved words). This can lead to cases where the editor generates a quoted FROM clause but the schema/fields metadata query still uses an unquoted table name (e.g., refId like "TABLE"). Use a single shared quoting helper for all SQL-expressions table/field quoting (and ideally handle reserved words + already-quoted identifiers).

cluster_summary: The read-back path never unquotes: Monaco tokenizes a backtick-quoted table name into separate tokens so getTableToken yields a lone backtick or quoted name, which fetchSQLFields re-quotes into broken SQL and whose refId filter matches nothing, so column autocomplete silently returns empty for the very refIds this change enables.
rationale: Monaco's mysql grammar emits the backtick as its own identifier.quote token, getTableToken returns it, fetchSQLFields re-quotes it and its refId filter matches nothing so column completion returns []; this is the production read-back defect thread 7 describes (quoted query.table vs raw refId lookup).
thread_body: These tests only verify the quoted SQL text, not the production flow where query.table is backtick-quoted but the backing query still has the raw refId. Because ExpressionQueryEditor passes { value: q.refId, label: q.refId }, we need a regression test that keeps queries[].refId unquoted while query.table is quoted; otherwise the missing source-query lookup in fetchSQLFields goes unnoticed.
